sections.h2: How do I sell my house fast in Cleburne, TX?
sections.html:
Most Cleburne owners who need speed sell directly to a cash buyer, and owners who can wait list with an agent. A direct sale skips showings, a buyer's loan and an appraisal, so it can close as soon as the title work is clear.

  • Direct cash sale: fits inherited houses, rentals with tenants, houses needing repairs and owners facing a foreclosure date.
  • Agent listing: fits a house in good repair and a seller with time to spare.
  • Sale by owner: fits a seller comfortable with contracts and buyer screening.

Cleburne is also the seat of Johnson County, and the Johnson County appraisal district keeps its office in the city.

sections.h2: What is Cleburne's history, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Cleburne began as a railroad and wagon-road town, and that background explains much of what makes it different from newer Dallas-Fort Worth suburbs. The Handbook of Texas places the city on U.S. Highway 67, thirty miles south of Fort Worth. The site sat near the earliest county road and had a good water source on West Buffalo Creek. It became a permanent settlement on March 23, 1867, when a central county seat was needed to replace Buchanan, and the town was named for a Confederate general. It incorporated in May 1871.

Rail made the town. A railroad line from Fort Worth through Cleburne to Temple opened in 1881, and in 1898 and 1899 the Santa Fe built its central machine shops here, which helped double the population in the 1890s. The population was 683 in 1870, 3,727 in 1890, 12,820 in 1920, and 26,005 in 2000. The same entry names Lake Pat Cleburne, the Layland Museum in the old Carnegie Library building, and the Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Station nearby as a major employer.

sections.h2: Where do I go for Cleburne property tax values and exemptions?
sections.html:
Values for Johnson County property come from the Central Appraisal District of Johnson County, at 109 N. Main St. in Cleburne, open Monday through Friday from 8:00am to 4:30pm, with a drop box at the front door. The office phone is (817) 648-3000, and exemption questions go to exemptions@johnsoncad.org.

The district posted that its 2026 certified appraisal data was available for download from August 10, 2026. It also reported a software upgrade during 2026 with dual data entry for a time, so confirm any exemption on your account directly with the district before you rely on an online screen.

The state calendar behind the bill is the same everywhere in Texas. Values are set as of January 1, and so is the lien. Notices of value for homesteads go out around April 1. The protest deadline is May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later. Bills arrive around October 1, and unpaid tax turns delinquent after January 31, as the Comptroller explains.

sections.h2: What exemptions can a Cleburne homeowner or buyer claim?
sections.html:
A Texas homeowner who lives in the house can claim a homestead exemption, and the school district portion is $140,000 under state law. The Comptroller lists the following extras:

  • Age 65 or older, or disabled: an additional $60,000 school exemption and a school tax ceiling.
  • Local option: a taxing unit may exempt up to 20 percent of value, with a minimum of $5,000.
  • Disabled veterans: exemption brackets that run from $5,000 for a 10 to 29 percent rating to $12,000 for 70 to 100 percent.
  • A 100 percent disabled veteran can receive a total exemption on a residence homestead.

Applications go to the appraisal district. The standard filing deadline is before May 1, though disabled veteran applicants can have up to five years after the delinquency date. A buyer who moves in after January 1 can often claim the exemption for the rest of that year if the seller did not hold it.

sections.h2: What should I check on permits and records before selling in Cleburne?
sections.html:
Ask the City of Cleburne's building inspections office whether any permit on your address is open or unfinished, and request the record in writing so you can hand it to the title company.

sections.h2: How does Texas handle foreclosure for a Cleburne house?
sections.html:
Texas foreclosures are mostly non-judicial, so a lender can sell a house at a courthouse auction without a lawsuit when the deed of trust has a power of sale. For a Cleburne house, that sale takes place in Johnson County. The borrower gets a notice of default and has 20 days from receiving it to reinstate by paying the past-due amount.

After that period, the lender sends a notice of sale at least 21 days before the sale. It must also be posted on the courthouse door and filed with the county clerk. The sale itself is a public auction held on the first Tuesday of a month between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m., and the Texas State Law Library says a federal rule generally bars starting foreclosure until a loan is over 120 days delinquent.

After the sale, a deficiency suit must be filed within two years, and the borrower may ask for a fair market value offset. Selling before the sale date can protect your equity and credit, so reach out early if you have received a notice.

sections.h2: What if the Cleburne house is inherited, has a tenant or needs a deed?
sections.html:
Each of these has a Texas rule that shapes how fast a sale can close.

  • Inherited: a will can be probated within four years of death. A muniment of title allows heirs to move title when no administration is needed. A small estate affidavit applies only when assets, apart from homestead and exempt property, are $75,000 or less and all heirs agree.
  • Tenant: a landlord typically gives at least 3 days of written notice to vacate, files in justice court and, after judgment, waits 6 days before a writ of possession can issue. An appeal to county court must be filed within 5 days of judgment.
  • Deed: the deed is recorded with the county clerk after it is signed and acknowledged before a notary, with fees of $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after.

Tell the buyer about each issue at the start. The title company will need proof of authority to sell, such as a court order or recorded affidavit.

faqs.q: Where is the Johnson County appraisal district office?
faqs.a: The Central Appraisal District of Johnson County is at 109 N. Main St. in Cleburne. It is open Monday through Friday from 8:00am to 4:30pm and can be reached at (817) 648-3000. A drop box is at the front door.

faqs.q: How old is the city of Cleburne?
faqs.a: Cleburne became a permanent settlement on March 23, 1867 and incorporated in May 1871, according to the Handbook of Texas. It replaced Buchanan as the Johnson County seat.

faqs.q: What is the Texas homestead exemption for school taxes?
faqs.a: School districts must give a $140,000 residence homestead exemption, per the Texas Comptroller. Owners 65 or older or disabled receive an additional $60,000 from the school district.

faqs.q: How much notice does a Texas foreclosure sale require?
faqs.a: The lender must give notice of sale at least 21 days before the sale, after the 20-day reinstatement period following the notice of default. Sales are held on the first Tuesday of the month.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cleburne house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers purchase as-is, and sellers disclose known problems. An open permit or code issue is the item most likely to need attention before closing, so ask Building Inspections what is on file.
